description: No CBK press-release / njoftime feed URL was pinned down in this pass, although press coverage clearly derives from one. Press releases are where instant-payment, SEPA and licensing milestones are first announced.

No confirmed public list of licensed payment institutions and e-money institutions as a distinct category (as opposed to the combined all-institutions PDF), and no confirmed register of registered payment service providers under the 2025 non-bank PSP access regulation.

CBK historical tender awards were only sampled (IT equipment 10 lots, mobile telephony, group life insurance). No systematic multi-year view of CBK IT / cash-handling / ATM / currency-processing awards and their winners was assembled.
No Serbian-language procurement terminology was searched (e.g. 'javne nabavke', 'obaveštenje o ugovoru', 'Centralna banka Kosova tender').

Neither the CBK material found nor the external reporting names the software vendor of KIPS itself (the existing RTGS/ACH), only the incoming Banca d'Italia TIPS-clone instant-payment layer. The incumbent switch/RTGS supplier for Kosovo remains unidentified.
The whole cell depends on one bot-defended domain (bqk-kos.org) plus one procurement portal with a history of multi-day outages (e-Prokurimi).

Serbian-language coverage of Kosovo procurement is effectively unaddressed: no sr-locale Kosovo source was reached, and no sr glossary of Kosovo-specific procurement terms was validated against live Kosovo documents.

Several named-in-scope buyers were not resolved to a concrete notice source: Posta e Kosoves, ATK (Administrata Tatimore e Kosoves, tax collection), KEK and water utilities, and the Kosovo Assembly's procurement directorate.
The exact OCDS API base URL and its auth/rate-limit behaviour for Kosovo PPRC were not captured — only the registry entry pointing to it.
No CPV-code filter set has been defined for banking, card, ATM/POS, treasury and payment IT within the Kosovo classification, so keyword-only filtering will over- and under-collect.
Pre-2016 procurement history predates e-Prokurimi and may only exist in prokurimihapur.org and the OSHP archive; continuity of the vendor time series is unverified.
It is not yet established whether ARBK's public search allows filtering by legal form (Dega e Shoqërisë së Huaj) or by activity code, or only by name/registration number.

No confirmed source for historical/time-series registry snapshots (when a vendor entity was first registered, ownership changes over time) beyond ARBK's own change history and Open Data Kosovo's 170k snapshot.
Serbian-language route into Kosovo registry data is unestablished; entities in the north may only appear in Serbian APR.
This pass mapped the registry infrastructure but did not yet resolve any specific banking/payments vendor to a Kosovo entity or branch (no actor-level lookups performed).
Whether Kosovo-registered entities must file public annual financial statements (and where those live, e.g. a financial reporting council) was not established.
No Albanian-language trade press or newsletter covering the Kosovo IT/systems-integration supply side (the vendors themselves) was identified — only general-news and investigative outlets.
None of the Albanian-language portals were confirmed to expose a stable archive/RSS interface, date-filtered search, or robots policy in this pass.
Turkish- and Bosnian-language Kosovo media were not covered by this cell's scope, despite TEB (Turkish-owned) being a major Kosovo bank and Turkish vendor ties being plausible.
Media reports name vendors and contract values but were not cross-linked to primary procurement records in this pass.
Several strong investigative hits (BQK tender award, KEK procurement) are historic; current-period (2024-2026) bank-technology contract reporting was sparse in results.

Serbian-side quasi-banking and cash-handling actors named in disputes (e.g. Jugobanka, Serbian Post/Pošta Srbije operations toward Kosovo, exchange offices/menjačnice in Serb-majority municipalities) were referenced only second-hand via KoSSev; no primary sites or registers were located for them.

No Serbian-language IT/vendor trade publication dedicated to payments technology was identified (equivalents of a 'PC Press'/'Mikro' style banking-IT desk); vendor signal currently rests almost entirely on eKapija.

Coverage skews to north Kosovo (Mitrovica-based outlets). Serb enclaves in central/southern Kosovo (Gračanica, Štrpce, Goraždevac) are covered only by Radio Kim and Goraždevac, whose banking/payments reporting depth is unverified.
No quantitative series was found for dinar cash volumes, dinar-account counts or dinar-denominated payment flows into Kosovo; NBS statistics cover Serbia as a whole without a Kosovo cut.
Serbian-language coverage clusters heavily around the Feb 2024 dinar-ban shock; continuity of the parallel payment arrangements through 2025-2026 was not established in this pass.

Vendor-side sponsorship and event pages (core banking / payments vendors such as Payten-Asseco SEE, Mellon, Transaction Systems, Natech, Printec-class integrators) were not scouted; these pages announce which Kosovo/WB events a vendor sponsors and often name the client bank.

LinkedIn event pages and post-event photo albums are where Kosovo sponsor logo walls, booth photos and speaker-affiliation lists actually live (KosICT, KBA, FIKS, AmCham Kosovo all post there), but were only touched via search snippets.
No Serbian-language Kosovo event source found; the sr dimension of this cell is covered only by Serbia-domestic proxies.
Only current/recent editions (2024-2027) of each event were mapped. Historical agendas and sponsor rosters — the trace showing when a vendor first appeared in Kosovo — were not retrieved.

University- and donor-run events (UBT International Conference, EBRD/IFC/USAID/LuxDev/GIZ-funded fintech workshops and demo days) were not scouted, though donor programmes frequently name both the bank and the implementing technology partner.
MTS d.o.o. (Telekom Srbija's Kosovo operation) and Serb-majority northern municipality utilities/billers were not covered.

No corporate-registry pointer captured. ARBK (Agjencia e Regjistrimit të Bizneseve në Kosovë) would give ownership, shareholder and beneficial-owner data for payment agents, retail chains and fuel networks.

Only one regional water company (KRU Prishtina) was captured; the remaining KRUs named by Capital Ria (Gjakova, Hidromorava, Hidroregjioni Jugor, and others) have their own billing systems and procurement.
No vendor-side case-study sources (terminal manufacturers, switch/acquiring software, kiosk vendors publishing Kosovo references) were identified in this slice.
e-Prokurimi's notice search may require registration or a digital certificate for anything beyond basic browsing, and no fetch was attempted to confirm what is publicly readable.
Individual MFI websites (KEP Trust, FINCA Kosovë, KRK, AFK, Besëlidhja, Kosinvest) were named via AMIK but not captured as individual sources.

EBRD, IFC and EIB Kosovo financial-sector diagnostics, technical cooperation project summaries and procurement notices were not searched (budget exhausted). These IFIs finance bank technology upgrades and publish project summaries naming beneficiaries.

Wayback recovery was validated as a method (CDX confirmed working for bqk-kos.org and e-prokurimi.rks-gov.net) but was not yet run against named vendor and commercial-bank domains to recover deleted reference/press pages.
CBK's own supervisory/annual audit of licensed banks and any published on-site examination summaries were not located; only the CBK's own audited statements and stability reports were found.

Albanian-language academic literature was reached only through two university repositories; Google Scholar / ResearchGate / DOAJ sweeps in Albanian ('pagesa elektronike', 'sistemi i pagesave', 'digjitalizimi bankar') were not performed.
IMF eLibrary PDF and Deloitte full reports may be gated or bot-defended; archive.today is expected to serve CAPTCHA to automated clients. None of these were confirmed dead — only presumed friction.
Serbian-language (sr) coverage of this cell is effectively empty; only English and Albanian sources were productively identified.
The access and licensing model of e-Prokurimi (Kosovo national e-procurement) was inferred from search summaries, not established by fetching the portal.
No sources identified for Kosovo commercial-bank-side donor-funded IT procurement (i.e. what a bank buys with an EBRD/IFC TA grant), which is typically not publicly tendered.
SECO (Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs) funds the IFC digital-financial-services programme with BQK, but no SECO reporting or procurement source was catalogued.
USAID Kosovo material is scattered across live and frozen archive hosts and UNDP purges expired notices, creating link rot in the donor-document trail.
No confirmed web domain was found for Ziraat Bank Kosovo, and Banka Ekonomike's and BPB's news/announcement feed URLs were inferred rather than confirmed.

Parent disclosure was confirmed only for ProCredit Holding and NLB Group. BKT's parent (BKT Albania / Çalık Holding), TEB's parents (BNP Paribas and Türk Ekonomi Bankası), Raiffeisen Bank International and Ziraat Bankası were not searched at parent level in this run; the RBI IR URL included above is inferred, not confirmed.
Serbian-language coverage of this cell is effectively empty, and Turkish (relevant for BKT, TEB and Ziraat parents) was not attempted at all.
Only current-page and recent-report layers were located; historical press-release archives (pre-2020) were not enumerated for any bank.
No RSS/Atom or JSON feed was confirmed for any of the eight bank newsrooms; only BPB is likely WordPress-backed.
The two anchor rosters in this cell (SHBK members, AMIK members) sit behind 403 responses to plain HTTP fetching.
Association event sponsor lists are ephemeral and edition-scoped; no historical series exists for SHBK Annual Banking Conference / Payments Forum or for KosICT.
Insurance-side industry body coverage rests on a third-party directory stub and the motor bureau; no association-owned member directory confirmed.
No Serbian-language association member directory for Kosovo was found; sr coverage of this cell is effectively limited to regulator locale pages.
STIKK's directory is tiered by sponsorship level and tagged by ~80 service specializations, but banking/payments specialization was not verified as a usable filter facet.
No association-level source found for Kosovo's savings-credit associations / non-bank financial institutions, and no separate fintech or payments-institution association was identified.
Membership rosters were inferred from search snippets and site structure, not read directly, for SHBK, AMIK and OEGJK.
Serbian-language sources covering payments and remittance channels in Serb-majority parts of Kosovo are essentially absent from this slice.
Telecom-led and post-office-led payment channels (Vala/IPKO mobile money, Posta e Kosovës financial services) were not systematically covered, although Posta appeared incidentally.
No procurement/tender source specific to payments infrastructure was captured beyond a single World Bank notice; Kosovo's national e-procurement platform was not searched.
The ICK startups directory and the FIKS member roster were identified as pointers but not enumerated into individual company sources within this pass.
Several corporate domains in this slice (onefor.com, swinto.com, stikk.org, arbk.rks-gov.net, ibas.world) were asserted from brand names or search snippets rather than fetched.
The processing/switching layer for Kosovo issuers and acquirers (in-house vs outsourced, and to whom) is unmapped.
No structured extraction yet of e-Prokurimi contract notices/awards relevant to self-service, terminals, cash handling and CIT.
Serbian-language coverage for this cell is thin: only directories and general regional outlets were found, no sr-language payments-industry source specific to Kosovo.
Cash-in-transit and ATM-replenishment operators in Kosovo are only partially identified (one insurer wording, one security firm); no licence register was located.
No source found that documents scheme certification status of terminals/processors in Kosovo (EMV/contactless/tokenisation certification lists).
Zero vendor-side references found for AML/transaction monitoring and for e-signature / PKI / qualified trust services at Kosovo institutions.
Albanian-language searching surfaced vendor announcements only via national media, not via vendor-owned pages; no Albanian-language vendor case-study library was located.

Several licensed Kosovo banks and the MFI/NBFI segment have no vendor pointer at all (Banka Ekonomike, Banka për Biznes beyond the Printec ATM post, TEB beyond the Printec ATM post, Ziraat Bank Kosova, Kosovo Savings & Credit associations, MFIs).

Vendor customer lists and case studies are routinely pruned; the current snapshot understates historical Kosovo wins (e.g. Comtrade's Kosovo references include institutions that no longer exist under those names, such as the Banking and Payments Authority of Kosovo and Kasabank).

The cell relies on vendors self-publishing, but the dominant pattern observed in Kosovo is that the vendor stays silent and evidence leaks through technical fingerprints (app package namespaces, e-banking URLs, certificate issuers) and local PR.
No Turkish-language searching was performed, despite Turkey being an explicit part of this cell's geography and Turkish-owned banks operating in Kosovo.
No Kosovo company register (ARBK / Agjencia e Regjistrimit të Bizneseve) source was located in this pass to enumerate the Kosovo subsidiaries and branches of regional integrators.

Hardware/self-service OEM channel (Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, Wincor legacy estate) partner directories for the Western Balkans were not enumerated, although Bankart's platform tender shows OEMs are decisive at the processing layer.
Regional ICT trade press and association directories outside Kosovo (MASIT in North Macedonia, AITA/PSHIK in Albania, Serbian and Croatian ICT clusters) were not yet profiled as pointer sources.
Vendor-to-bank attribution in Kosovo rests largely on inference; no systematic reverse-lookup of the eleven Kosovo commercial banks' technology stacks has been done.
Two useful sources (D&B profiles, LinkedIn company pages) are paywalled or ToS-restricted, limiting automated sizing of competitor Kosovo operations.
Kosovo job postings are removed at deadline and are poorly archived, so historical hiring-burst analysis is impossible retroactively.
Serbian-language coverage for northern Kosovo rests on two Serbia-hosted boards; no Kosovo-Serb local board or municipal vacancy channel was identified.
Bank-owned careers pages were not enumerated in this pass; many Kosovo banks post technical roles only on their own site, bypassing the boards entirely.
RFP-adjacent signals were only approached through PM job ads; no procurement/tender surface was covered in this cell (it belongs to another cell but the join is essential).
APK/SDK fingerprinting was identified as a method but no Kosovo bank APK was actually analysed, so no concrete SDK evidence exists yet.
